title: Go Defer, Panic, Recover: Core Control Flow

scenes.say: Ever crashed a Go app? How do you recover from unexpected errors in Go?

scenes.label: defer
scenes.sub: Runs code after your function returns. Great for cleanup.
scenes.say: Defer lets you schedule code to run after your function returns. It's perfect for cleanup tasks, like closing files.

scenes.label: panic
scenes.sub: Raises a runtime error. Stops normal flow.
scenes.say: Panic raises a runtime error and stops normal control flow. It's how Go signals something went seriously wrong.
Here, defer sets up a function to catch a panic. If panic is called, recover grabs it and prints recovered, so the program doesn't crash.

scenes.question: Should you always use recover?
scenes.right: No, use recover only for unexpected panics, not for regular error handling.
scenes.say: Here's a common trap: should you always use recover? No way. Only use recover for unexpected panics, not for regular errors.
